## Generalized Linear Model

This section was lead by Benjamin Jud.\
Using a Poisson Generalized Linear Model, we will examine count data on arrivals and overnights in xxx...\
\
First, lets examine the two columns:

```{r}
summary(swiss_hotel_panel[, c("arrivals", "overnights")])
```

From the summary call, we can see that both columns consist of integer values greater than 0. As such, we can model this count data using poisson and quasi-poisson models. We can also see that there is quite data is generally left skewed, with a long rightsided tail. As such, both `Arrivals` and `Overnights` will be log-transformed.

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(log(swiss_hotel_panel$arrivals), main = 'Histogram of Arrivals', xlab = 'Arrivals (log transformed)')
hist(log(swiss_hotel_panel$overnights), main = 'Histogram of Overnights', xlab = 'Overnights (log transformed)')
```
